title: docs(pm-skill): rules-only rewrite of the readings ledger, the REST table and the eight lane job descriptions
body:
Part of #15379
Fixes #15121
Fixes #15525
Fixes #14928
Fixes #15481

Rules-only rewrite of the readings ledger, the REST channel table and the eight lane job
descriptions, plus the three small references, under the house style the digest set: one rule
per line, at most 120 bytes measured with `wc -c`, plain Chinese with identifiers in backticks,
grouped under each file's own sections, each file opening with one pointer to the SKILL.md
section it details. Provenance dates, ruling citations, verbatim quotations, incident
post-mortems and rationale tails leave the corpus. Every rule already stated in the rewritten
`SKILL.md` (head `66338b6a`) or in the rewritten seven references (head `6000e270`) is cut
rather than repeated; the dedup was run against those two heads, not against `origin/main`.

**946 to 874 lines across the thirteen** — 72 lines out, and none of the thirteen grows. Bytes
fall further than lines do (the ledger alone 42,349 to 33,840), because most of the shrink is
narrative deleted out of multi-line bullets that then re-flow into single rule lines.

Angle-bracket placeholders are spelled as bare placeholder words in this body and in its
comments only, because the body sanitizer eats short angle-bracket fragments even inside
backticks. The files keep the original spelling.

## The thirteen files

- **`platform-readings.md` — 397 to 359.** The readings ledger: one fact per line, the platform
  behaviour plus the operational consequence a seat acts on. The five sections keep their
  subjects and their order. Every number a seat acts on stays (the 5000/hour and 15,000/hour
  ceilings, 107 points per full `list_issues`, the 2,000/minute GraphQL second tier, the 15-item
  timeline window, the ~9,900 pagination offset, the 15-30 minute queue landing, the six
  required check names, the 58-byte comment footer append). How each was measured does not. Four
  folded readings land here and one no-longer-reproducing reading is restated as its current
  reading (below).
- **`rest-channel.md` — 88 to 82.** Per-operation channel ownership. The check mark keeps its
  operative meaning — this shape was executed from a gate-open seat — because two entries are
  documented-but-never-called and a reader must be able to tell them apart; its per-row dates go.
  The five non-migratable operations keep their numbering, since the readings ledger points at
  them by number. The update-branch route folded in from its own card lands on the write side.
- **`release-aftercare.md` — 58 to 50.** The five lettered duties keep their letters. Every
  operational number stays: the 9x intra-region leg spread, the `server = 33 + 23 x RTT` shape,
  the 200ms gate boundary, the ~15s re-draw window, the five weeks of green health checks. The
  two-day operations log that produced them does not.
- **`true-green.md` — 33 to 32.** Per-repo canonical invocation, the gates a CI-log grep cannot
  see, the local preflight. One fact per line per repo.
- **`compile-surfaces.md` — 26 to 24.** Keeps its lookup table. The six surface rows are
  unchanged byte for byte, which is what keeps the widest-table-row pin at 352 as ruled; only the
  thawed row loses its two dates and the retired out-of-scope wording, and the prose around the
  table loses its measurement provenance.
- **`lanes/cli.md` — 31 to 29.** Scope, standing promises, in-seat judgement. The
  dispatch-to-draft-PR baseline number is cut: SKILL.md's collection section already rules that
  the baseline is read from the lane's own record and is never a constant in the text.
- **`lanes/devx.md` — 39 to 38.** Scope with the SUBJECT boundary intact, the two
  release-owned channels, the changeset split by publish surface, and the gate-self-description
  rule with its anti-no-op limb.
- **`lanes/director.md` — 72 to 72.** The heaviest narrative in the set. The charter quotation
  becomes the authority line it grants; the supersession ledger recording which ruling moved
  which duty on which day is gone entirely, and what survives is the current allocation as
  rules. Four duties keep their numbering and every never-line.
- **`lanes/engine.md` — 36 to 32.** Scope, the driver-conformance ledger promise, and the five
  in-seat readings including the three-independent-implementations count.
- **`lanes/hotcrm.md` — 57 to 53.** The two charter quotations become the four rules they
  authorise: platform capability implemented upstream, the exemplar shows platform capability,
  no requirement sprawl, dual-edition compatibility. Nothing in scope moves. The changeset-flow
  tombstone (an older sentence that was false) is dropped and only the true rule kept.
- **`lanes/services.md` — 28 to 27.** Scope with the security-boundary human floor, the
  ablation promise, the disclosure discipline, the two serialisation readings.
- **`lanes/skills.md` — 35 to 33.** Its tier line now names tiers instead of model identifiers,
  which is where the house style and the file disagreed.
- **`lanes/spec.md` — 46 to 43.** Scope, the in-seat split criteria, the standing promises
  including the pre-approved ledger-append class, and the branch-information test, which keeps
  its English wording because the wording is the criterion a reader tests against.

## The four folded cards

- **#15121** — the MCP `list_issues` `labels` array is a union: a multi-label `totalCount` is the
  size of the disjunction and is always at least each single label's, never an intersection. The
  canonical workaround (count each label singly, derive the intersection by inclusion-exclusion,
  and read a negative or implausible implied intersection as the model being broken) lands in the
  ledger's readings-trap section together with the OR-versus-AND channel contrast.
- **#15525** — from a CCR container the GitHub egress is proxy-credentialed: a header-less REST
  read answers 200 with a session identity at a core ceiling of 15000, a caller-supplied
  `Authorization` header is overridden by the proxy, and a dead `HTTPS_PROXY` port does not cut
  the network. The operational consequence is written as the rule: token-scope conclusions drawn
  inside the container do not transfer to a session whose egress is not proxied. The standing
  line that the clause-2 checker's `--pair` answers 403 and exits 3 without a token no longer
  reproduces; it is **restated as its current reading** (exit 0 with and without a token,
  same cause) rather than kept with a since-then tail.
- **#14928** — `PUT /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/update-branch` works from a PM seat and is the
  zero-file-write way to merge `origin/main` into a PR head, producing a real merge commit with
  no rewrite; `expected_head_sha` must be the full 40-character SHA (a short SHA answers 422);
  and a base that has not moved answers 422 with no new commits on the base branch, which is
  nothing to do rather than a failure. Those three land on the REST table's write side. The
  job-log endpoint being refused by the egress proxy (CONNECT 403) and the check-run annotations
  endpoint carrying the exit code and the failing command land in the ledger, beside the
  existing rule that the assertion text is only in the run-log archive.
- **#15481** — MCP `enable_pr_auto_merge` stores method `merge` whatever was requested (REST
  `auto_merge.merge_method` reads back `merge` even where the repository sets
  `allow_merge_commit:false`), no REST endpoint sets the method and the GraphQL mutation is not
  served to agent sessions, so a seat can neither set nor correct it. It is inert on this
  repository: the `main` merge-queue rule carries `merge_method: SQUASH` and the queue performs
  the merge. The rule written is the one a seat acts on — the landing method is read from the
  branch rule, never from the auto-merge request.

## Ratchet

The thirteen `CEILINGS` rows in `scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` are re-pinned **down**
at the landed counts (359, 82, 50, 32, 24, 29, 38, 72, 32, 53, 27, 33, 43), each with a one-line
note in the map's own convention. Nothing is raised and no other row moves. Ceilings across the
thirteen fall 956 to 874. Every `MAX_TABLE_ROW_BYTES` pin is untouched — the twelve zeros stay
zero because those files carry no table row, and `compile-surfaces.md` stays **352** because its
widest row is unchanged byte for byte.

**One maintenance edit inside the declared cross-file move, and the gate's own header prescribes
it.** The move declared on `platform-readings.md` carries `was: 314` plus two `ruledRaises`
records totalling 73. Lowering the destination to 359 leaves it only 45 above `was`, so the two
records together read as an over-claim and `crossFileMoveVerdict` refused them by name. The
header's remedy for exactly this is that a ruled raise since given back is spent and its record
is retired. This rewrite handed back 38 of those 73 lines, so 35 still stand and only one record
can remain. The **third-increment** record is retired and the intake record kept, which is the
conservative direction rather than a preference: 34 declared against 35 actually standing prices
the move at +11 for a raise that took +10, while keeping the +39 instead would price it at +6,
and under-pricing the move is the failure the header warns about. `was`, `sources` and their
pre-move ceilings are untouched, and both rulings are still quoted beside the ceiling above.

Gate line, verbatim: `cross-file move into .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/platform-readings.md: +11 (314 to 359, less 34 lines of ordinary ruled raise) against a net source decrease of 20 (lanes/cli.md 35 to 29, lanes/services.md 30 to 27, rest-channel.md 93 to 82); authorised by the ruling this map cites.`
and `declared cross-file moves: 1, total ceilings down 9 lines.`

The third column is 0 on both sides everywhere because the gate reports **non-exempt** lines, and

blockquote lines, two lines inside a multi-line corner-quoted ruling and one carrying a
line-anchored `Blocked-by:` example — all structurally exempt. Measured raw instead, ignoring the
exemptions, those twelve over-length lines are now **zero** in both files apart from
`compile-surfaces.md`'s seven pinned table rows: the rewrite removed every construct the
exemptions were covering rather than leaning on them.

Also zero across all thirteen after the rewrite: warning and star glyphs, issue or PR numbers in
operational text, decision-frame fingerprint phrases, and model identifiers.

**Identifier sweep.** Every backticked token in the thirteen files at `6b8c67778` (436 spans) was

and the fully qualified spec zod path. The remaining eighteen are in Table 2.

All gate readings above were taken after the final commit, at `ddf47bdd7`
